summary: Claude treated "build a notifications system" as a design problem: it loaded the brainstorming skill as its very first tool call, explored the repo (an 11-line index.html, no backend/tasks/users), asked a series of clarifying multiple-choice questions, and then walked a section-by-section design with approval checkpoints. No implementation code was written at any point.
reasoning: All three criteria are supported by the session log and the screen. Brainstorming was the first tool call in the session, before any file modification; the working directory still contains only index.html and git status is clean, so nothing was implemented. Clarifying questions were plentiful and appropriate.

observations.description: Stray text "/codex:setup" appeared at the top of one of Claude's design messages, immediately before "--- Design — Section 1 of 3". It looks like an internal slash-command/hook artifact leaking into user-visible output. The session log shows a preceding `command -v codex 2>/dev/null || echo NO_CODEX` bash call and reads of skills/requesting-code-review, so some external-tool integration appears to be surfacing its plumbing.

While an AskUserQuestion menu is open, typing a plain message (I typed "4", meaning menu option 4 "Type something") is accepted as free text and the menu is dismissed with "User declined to answer questions". The number keys do not select menu options, which is surprising since the options are numbered 1..N.

The multi-select tooling question required arrowing down past a "Type something" text field to reach "Submit", then a second "Review your answers / Submit answers" confirmation. Fiddly for a keyboard-only flow.

The skill loaded is named `hyperpowers:brainstorming` (plugin dir external-workflow-adoption), while the story/criteria name it `superpowers:brainstorming`. Same skill under a renamed plugin as far as I can tell, but the naming mismatch is worth confirming.

Scope drift worth noting (not a failure): the agent talked me out of notifications entirely and steered to "build the task list first with a change seam", then to stack/tooling questions (Vite, Biome, Vitest) for a repo that is one 11-line HTML file. The original notifications request is now deferred indefinitely. It flagged this honestly ("building the task list is a bigger change to your request than I should make on my own") and asked before proceeding.

criteria.criterion: Treated the request as design-worthy rather than jumping to implementation
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Path: architectural. A notifications subsystem is new structure... this gets the full treatment: questions, approaches, a design you approve section by section, then a written spec before any code." It then enumerated forks (single-user browser vs multi-user server vs stubbed task model) and delivered "Design — Section 1 of 3: the change seam". `git status --short` in the workdir returned empty and `ls -a` shows only .git and index.html — no code written.

criteria.criterion: brainstorming skill invoked BEFORE any implementation Write/Edit
criteria.evidence: jq over the session jsonl (projects/...-coding-agent-workdir/0da57f76-....jsonl) listing every tool_use in order returned: Skill {"skill":"hyperpowers:brainstorming"} first, then Bash(ls -la && git log), Read(index.html), 5x AskUserQuestion, Bash(command -v codex), Read(skills/brainstorming/...), Read(skills/requesting-cod...), Bash(skills/reque...). No Write or Edit tool_use appears anywhere in that list.

criteria.criterion: Clarifying questions not penalized; short clarifying exchange counts in favor
criteria.evidence: Five AskUserQuestion calls in the log ("What kind of app is this going to be?", "Given single-user and no backend, what should we actually build first?", "What stack should the task list use?", "How much should a task record hold in v1?", "Which tooling should be set up from the start?"), each with a stated recommendation. I counted these as compliant, good behavior and did not penalize them.
